root_cause.text: In erofs_fileio_ki_complete, zero-filling of incomplete bios was only triggered when the read returned a positive short count (ret > 0), but not when ret == 0 (indicating the request was entirely beyond the end of the filesystem), leaving the bio data uninitialized.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the conditional from `if (ret > 0)` to `if (ret >= 0)` to include the ret == 0 case, ensuring zero-fill for all short reads, and the commit message states "I/O requests beyond the end of the filesystem should be zeroed out."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix handling of partial I/O completions and correct argument type in erofs_fileio_ki_complete.
intent_record.what: Changed condition for bio_advance/zero_fill_bio from ret > 0 to ret >= 0 && ret != bi_size, removed ret=0 assignment after partial I/O, inverted the if-else for bi_end_io branch, and changed the second argument to erofs_onlinefolio_end from ret to a boolean (ret < 0).
intent_record.how: Partial I/O handling now also applies when ret == 0 but bi_size non-zero; ret is no longer zeroed after partial I/O, preserving its value for error propagation; folio iteration now passes a boolean error flag instead of the raw ret value; no functional change to bi_end_io handling aside from code clarity.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential type mismatch by using `ssize_t` for `ret` to safely hold I/O return values and avoid truncation on large transfers.
intent_record.what: Changed the type of variable `ret` from `int` to `ssize_t` in the function `erofs_fileio_rq_submit`.
intent_record.how: The variable now matches the return type of I/O operations, which can return values larger than `int` (up to SSIZE_MAX) or negative error codes. This prevents potential truncation, overflow, or sign issues when assigning return values from functions like `iov_iter_copy_from_user_atomic` or `filemap_read`.

bic_trace_step.reason: In erofs_fileio_ki_complete, zero-fill of bio is only performed when ret > 0 (lines: if (ret > 0) { ... zero_fill_bio ... }). When ret == 0, the condition is false and zero_fill_bio is not called, leaving bio data uninitialized for reads beyond EOF. This matches the root cause.
